title: skyBlip flight log record (v1)
description: ONE decoded record out of a flight, as a host decoder reads it off the log endpoint's base64 chunks. The firmware owns the layout (firmware/core/flight/log_record.h): 24 bytes, little-endian, bytes 0-1 the seconds since the session opened, bytes 22-23 a CRC-16-CCITT over the first 22, every field written one at a time. A session holds fixes, one a second while the aircraft flies and the minute before its takeoff, and events beside them: a status a minute and whenever the cell changes level, an alarm whenever a target's level changes, and an encounter, the closest pass of each aircraft heard, written when it leaves the table or the flight ends. Records are in the order they were written, not the order they describe. Every record carries type and utc_s; the rest of the keys belong to the type named at the front of each description and no record mixes two of them. A session listed closed:false ended with the power: its last record may be a torn write, which the CRC refuses.

type.description: What this record is. A fix carries byte 16 as the high byte of its nine-bit track, so the byte is 0 or 1; an event sets its top bit and names its kind in the other seven: status=0x81, alarm=0x82, encounter=0x83. A kind is retired, never renumbered, because a flight on the partition outlives the firmware that wrote it.

utc_s.description: Every type. The UTC second this record describes: the session id, which is the first second of the session, plus the 16-bit offset in bytes 0-1, saturating 18 hours in. An encounter is dated at its closest approach, so it is written after records later than it: sort by utc_s, not by index. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'utc'

latitude_1e7.description: fix. Latitude, 1e-7 degrees, bytes 2-5. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'lat_1e7'

longitude_1e7.description: fix. Longitude, 1e-7 degrees, bytes 6-9. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'lon_1e7'

altitude_msl_m.description: fix. Altitude above mean sea level, metres, bytes 10-11. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'alt_msl_m'

altitude_hae_m.description: fix. Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid, metres: altitude_msl_m plus the signed geoid separation in byte 12. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'alt_hae_m'

speed_q.description: fix. Ground speed in quarter metres per second, the ADS-L G.1.8 unit, bytes 13-14

speed_mm_s.description: fix. speed_q in millimetres per second

track_c9.description: fix. Track over the ground on the 512-unit circle of ADS-L G.1.10, bytes 15-16

track_deg.description: fix. track_c9 in whole degrees, rounded as core/units does

climb_e8.description: fix. Vertical speed in eighths of a metre per second, the ADS-L G.1.9 unit, bytes 17-18. Meaningless unless climb_valid

climb_mm_s.description: fix. climb_e8 in millimetres per second

satellites.description: fix. Satellites in the solution, byte 19. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'sats'

hdop_e2.description: fix. Horizontal dilution of precision in hundredths, stored in tenths in byte 20

flight_state.description: fix. The ADS-L G.1.2 flight state when the fix was taken, bits 5-6 of byte 21. Codes: 0 unknown, 1 on_ground, 2 airborne

pps_locked.description: fix. Bit 2 of byte 21: the clock was disciplined to the receiver's PPS

geoid_measured.description: fix. Bit 4 of byte 21: the receiver reported the geoid separation rather than the device assuming one

session_end.description: fix. Bit 7 of byte 21: the landing's last record. A session whose last record does not carry it ended with the power

cell_mv.description: status. The cell's voltage in millivolts when valid, what the divider last read otherwise, bytes 2-3

percent.description: status. State of charge the gauge shows, byte 4

power_level.description: status. core/power's cutoff level, byte 5. Codes: 0 unknown, 1 normal, 2 critical, 3 flat, 4 low, the same as the diagnostics power record. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'level'

charge.description: status. Whether the die temperature allowed charging, byte 6. Codes: 0 unknown, 1 ok, 2 too_cold, 3 too_hot

tracked.description: status. Aircraft in the traffic table at this second, byte 7

tracked_peak.description: status. The most aircraft in the table at once since the previous status, byte 8

battery_valid.description: status. Bit 0 of byte 9: cell_mv and percent are the cell's. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'valid'

external_power.description: status. Bit 2 of byte 9: the cable is in

address.description: alarm, encounter. The aircraft's 24-bit address, bytes 2-4

address_mapping_table.description: alarm, encounter. The address table it belongs to, byte 5

distance_m.description: alarm, encounter. Horizontal distance in metres, both positions carried to the same instant, bytes 6-7. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'dist_m'

relative_altitude_m.description: alarm, encounter. Its altitude above own-ship, metres, bytes 8-9. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'rel_alt_m'

relative_bearing_deg.description: alarm, encounter. Bearing to it, degrees clockwise from own-ship's track, bytes 10-11. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'rel_bearing_deg'

closing_mps.description: alarm, encounter. Closing speed, metres per second, positive closing, bytes 12-13

alarm.description: alarm, encounter. On an alarm the level the target just took, on an encounter the highest it reached: 0 none, 1 advisory, byte 14

aircraft_category.description: alarm, encounter. Its ADS-L G.1.3 aircraft category, byte 15. Captures fetched before #151 name it 'aircraft_cat'

source.description: alarm, encounter. Which path it was heard on, byte 17. Codes: 0 adsl_direct, 1 adsl_uplink, 2 alptas, 3 own

rssi_dbm.description: alarm, encounter. Signal strength of the reception, byte 18

dismissed.description: alarm, encounter. Bit 0 of byte 19: the pilot had dismissed its alarm

in_formation.description: alarm, encounter. Bit 1 of byte 19: flying in formation with own-ship, so its alarm was withheld

heard_s.description: encounter. Seconds from the first assessment of this aircraft to the last, bytes 20-21
